sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: Lord Buddha is depicted ______ and in human form in Ajanta paintings.
The Ajanta caves are located near ______ district in Maharashtra.
The depiction of ______ is particularly noteworthy in Ajanta.
The Black Princess is a testament to the artist's ______.
The colours used in Ajanta paintings are simple and ______, not loud.

sections.passage: The Ajanta caves are located near Aurangabad district in Maharashtra. Ajanta paintings hold a unique place in the history of Indian painting. Buddha is depicted in symbolic and human forms in Ajanta paintings. The Ajanta paintings were created in Buddhist stupas and chaityas, and the depiction of women is particularly noteworthy. Black Princess is considered one of the finest works among the Ajanta paintings: the free lines, the delicate harmony of the body parts, the slight tilt of the face and the curves of the eyes show the artist's mastery. The colours used are very simple and earthy and not loud. (April 2026)

sections.title: Read the passage and state whether each statement is true or false.

questions.q: The Gupta period is regarded as the golden period of Indian art history.
Sarnath and Mathura were art centres in the Gupta period.
The slight tilt of the lip is a stylistic feature of the Guptas.
Temple architecture started at Udaygiri in Gujarat.
questions.answer: False – the Udaygiri caves and Nachna and Bhumara are in Madhya Pradesh.

sections.passage: The Gupta period is regarded as the golden period of Indian art history. Refinement came in the representation of the human figures. Some of the most important art centres during this period were Mathura, Sarnath, Ujjain and Ahichhatra. The slight tilt of the lip, the full roundness of the figures, accurate carvings and simplicity became the stylistic stamp of the Guptas. Famous paintings of Ajanta were done during this period. The Udaygiri caves in Madhya Pradesh and the places Nachna and Bhumara show the beginning of temple architecture. (October 2025)

questions.q: Describe the base and material of the Bull Capital.
questions.answer: The base is an inverted bell-shaped lotus with an abacus above it carrying plant designs; the capital is made of polished sandstone and is about 7 ft high.

questions.q: Describe the Surasundari from Konarka.
questions.answer: It is a little more than life-size stone figure of a female musician from the 12th-century Sun temple in Orissa, shown with a drum. The big smiling face, slight tilt of the head, rhythmic limbs, soft carving of ornaments and folds of drapery give graceful beauty and rhythm.

questions.q: What are the characteristic features of Rembrandt's paintings?
questions.answer: Rembrandt was a Dutch realist; his paintings show the mysteries in the play of light and shade which highlights the soul of the painting, and he painted traditional portraits with expression.

questions.q: Explain the painting 'Landscape in Red'.
questions.answer: F.N. Souza's 'Landscape in Red' (oil, 1961) is an experimental cityscape showing a city as a concrete jungle with a mysterious character. Calligraphic lines are arranged with colours; red predominates with a few splashes of green; no rule of perspective is followed yet depth of space is clearly shown.

sections.title: Short answer question. Answer in 50–60 words.

questions.q: Briefly describe Salvador Dali's contribution to Surrealism.
questions.answer: Dali was the most famous Surrealist painter, a Spanish painter, film maker and writer. He used a highly realistic, academic and precise technique to depict the world of absurd, strange and dream-like elements and an unconventional grouping of objects with symbolic meaning. 'Persistence of Memory', 'Small Bottle of Rum' and 'Honey is Sweeter than Blood' are his works.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 70–80 words.

questions.q: Write a note on Hoysala art with reference to the Krishna Govardhana sculpture.
questions.answer: The Hoysala style (mid 11th–mid 14th century) developed in the Deccan with capital Dvarasamudra (Halebid); major temples are at Belur, Halebid and Somnathpur. Temples were decorated with sculptures that form part of the architecture. The soft stone allowed deep carving and undercutting, soft rhythms and intricate details. The Krishna Supporting Mount Govardhana from Belur (about 3 ft) shows Krishna as the central heroic figure with humans and cattle in layers, lively animals, heavy breasts and buttocks, rich jewellery and typical hairstyle, showing the artist's mastery.
